annotations.title: What life phase (dasha) someone is in and what changes next

description: Explains the life phase a person is in right now, what it tends to bring, when it ends and what comes next, from their birth details; or, without birth details, what a given phase means in general and how long it lasts. Useful when the user wonders why life feels a certain way at the moment, when things will change, or about timing for career, marriage, a move or a fresh start, for themselves or someone close to them. Also for direct questions: "what's my dasha", "which mahadasha am I in", "what's coming in my dasha", "meri dasha kaunsi chal rahi hai", "Shani ki mahadasha kab khatam hogi", "mera time kab badlega". Uses the Vimshottari dasha system. Two ways to call it: (1) with birth details (date, time, place) it returns the running Mahadasha and Antardasha with exact start/end dates, what the period is about for that chart and the next antardashas (AstroCalc engine); or (2) with lord (and optionally antardasha) set to a planet, e.g. lord "Saturn", antardasha "Venus", it returns the general meaning and length of that period, with no birth data needed. Birth details are not stored. Traditional information, not a prediction.

antardasha.description: Optional antardasha (sub-period) planet inside lord, e.g. "Venus".

lang.description: Language of the text fields: 'en' (English, default) or 'hi' (Hindi).

lat.description: Birth latitude in decimal degrees (north positive). Give together with lon.

lon.description: Birth longitude in decimal degrees (east positive). Give together with lat.

lord.description: Mahadasha planet for a general explanation: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu or Ketu (Hindi/Sanskrit names like Shani or Guru also work). Ignored when date is given.

place.description: Birth city or town, e.g. 'Lucknow' or 'Pune, Maharashtra, India'. The best match is used (Indian cities preferred); call search_place first if unsure. Not needed when lat and lon are given.

time.description: Local clock time of birth, 24-hour HH:MM (e.g. '06:45', '21:10'); '6:45 am' / '9:10 PM' also work. Use 'unknown' (or omit) if not known: noon is used, the Moon sign stays reliable but the Lagna is approximate.
